system.summary: Letter table with 2-3 homophones per common letter, doubled letters written as numbers, nulls (signs and clear Latin words) and a few code signs: rho with a numeral, H with a 9. About 55 signs. No word division.
system.doubled_letters: numbers: 3 cc, 5 ff, 6 gg, 7 ll, 8 mm, 9 pp, 10 rr, 11 ss, 14 nn
system.notes: Codes: Q3 Hamet, Q4 Bassa Budensis, Q6 Transiluania, Q8 Lippa, H9 exercitus; Q7 not identified. Nulls: Ex, Eo, epsilon, n:, m:, d:, q:, the double-barred 6, +Th, and clear words Sicut, Insuper, Postq; 130 of 1904 signs. Same family as malvezzi1548 and huyson1547, but those keys do not apply.

His files were not seen. Veress, Documente I (1929), Nos. 135 and 137 print excerpts of the 18 and 22 Oct letters; the 15 Oct letter is not there. Other editions and the Vienna minute were not checked (3 Nov 2026).

solution.what: ff. 9r-15v and 34r-48v of G 275 inf. fetched from the Ambrosiana IIIF service, one request at a time.
Ledger, Carpentieri 2012 and two web searches; Dudout notes in research/dudout_2026-10-29/ read. Veress not opened yet.
Cipher lines of ff. 9r-10r and 34r-35v cut into shapes, clustered with no language, named by eye, labelled by a nearest-neighbour classifier (pass A).
Pass A of ff. 9r-9v aligned with the gloss of 9r-9v by EM. As run, 14 sign values were fixed in every restart and seven nulls were set by hand afterwards. Frozen as key_frozen.tsv.
Held-out f. 10r: frozen table on raw machine labels against the gloss, 442 of 518 letters in order (85.3%); shuffled tables best 41.5%.
Pass B: ff. 34r-35v read by eye on strips, not blind.
Decrypted and read; Hh, ii and 7 changed after the freeze with reasons in key.tsv.

Independent blind check (VERIFY.md): f. 34r, 350 signs, 6 differences (1.7%), 0 after zoom; own table from random starts gave 303 of 334 letters of its blind 34r. Found one phantom sign and a misdescribed method.
Corrections applied on the images: phantom sign at 35r.11 removed; doubtful signs marked at 34v.06, 35r.24, 35r.27. One disagreement with the check logged: the numeral at 34v.06 is nearer 8 than 5.
EM rerun with no seed values: locked at restart 21, all 36 frozen letter values the same.
Q7: margins, top and foot bands of 29 glossed pages read by eye; rho signs sought by a shape filter (11 found, none with a 7).
Veress, Documente I (1929), opened: no letter of 15 Oct; Nos. 135 and 137 print excerpts of the 18 and 22 Oct letters.

outcome.method_basis: Table built by aligning machine labels of ff. 9r-9v with the contemporary gloss of the same pages, then frozen and tested on held-out f. 10r. The sister letters are the adjacent plaintext; the 15 Oct letter has no decipherment of its own.
outcome.fraction_read_source: The 15 Oct letter is 82 cipher lines of roughly 530 in the four letters, a rough count of lines from a machine pass that includes some clear text. That letter reads at 316 of 317 words.

texts.label: 15 Oct 1552, ff. 34r-36r
texts.summary: Ferdinand would have liked a demonstration towards Lippa to draw the Ottoman army off Eger and to support Maurice of Saxony. He sends money and cloth, tells Castaldo to hold soldiers and subjects to their duty, and expects the enemy to be drawn off or driven off by winter.
texts.note: Words 317: 316 read as sense, 311 with no restored or changed letter, 306 with every doubtful sign out as well. One code word, Q7, is open.

reading_review.by: AI language-model agent (for WAINUT; a model reading, not a person), independent of the solver
reading_review.note: Read as sentences 3 Nov 2026. The cipher section reads as eight complete, grammatical Latin sentences with a clear argument: a wished-for feint towards Lippa to draw the Turks off Eger, money and cloth for the soldiers, and an order to hold soldiers and subjects to their duty until winter drives the enemy off. The decryption matches the reading letter for letter apart from four marked slips or missing letters (habemes, singslari, rationibu, diutiu), and the English follows the Latin faithfully. The real holes are few: code word Q7 is filled from context only (shown as ?Themeswar), the second Lippa rests on a doubtful numeral, a handful of single letters stand on blotted or faint signs, and the code values (Lippa, exercitus, Hamet, Transylvania) come from the sister letters' glosses rather than from a decipherment of this letter.
